## IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1422 (pushed, awaiting gates)

Removal executed per the recorded operator ruling. Verification summary:

### What was removed
- `CodeHealthConfig.enabled` (the field) and its `_SECTIONS` coercion row, in
  `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`.
- `enabled` from both `[code_health]` TOML examples and the type prose in `docs/config.md`.
- The `enabled` assertions / CLI override / golden-surface expectations in the two
  `test_code_health_config*` files, and `enabled` from the documented-keys tuple in
  `tests/scripts/test_metrics_docs.py`.

Also corrected a docs claim NOT in the original scope but squarely inside the AC "the docs no
longer advertise an off switch that does not exist": the `code_health.*` section opened with
"Code-health analysis is inert by default", which is precisely the false advertisement this bug
is about. It now states there is no on/off switch and that these keys only *tune* the analysis.
The `CodeHealthConfig` docstring ("Inert-by-default analyzer selection...") was corrected for
the same reason.

### Tombstone — RUNTIME-verified, not verified by inspection
Two warn-class tombstones added (`code_health.enabled` cfg + `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` env).
All THREE input channels were exercised against a real project and each WARNs and exits 0:

| channel | result |
|---|---|
| `rebar.toml` `[code_health] enabled = true` | `WARNING rebar: code_health.enabled was removed in v1.0.0 (no replacement; it is now ignored)`, exit 0 |
| `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED=true` env | same warning on the env name, exit 0 |
| `-c code_health.enabled=true` CLI override | same warning, exit 0 |
| `rebar config validate` | `WARN: cfg code_health.enabled was removed in v1.0.0`, exit 0 |

The surviving keys still apply alongside the warning (`size_cap = 800` was read back
correctly), so the tombstone does not poison the rest of the section.

### RED to GREEN
Two new tests in `tests/unit/test_config_backcompat.py` (the existing home of tombstone/warn
tests). Both were confirmed RED *before* the tombstones existed, and for the right reasons:

- cfg case: without the tombstone it raised `ConfigError` under `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error`
  (the generic unknown-key path). That strict policy is deliberately what makes the test
  discriminating — a run that merely warns and returns a config proves the TOMBSTONE fired, not
  the unknown-key path.
- env case: without the tombstone the warning list was EMPTY — the total silence that is exactly
  the silent-drop being prevented.

Restoring the tombstones turned both GREEN. This doubles as the mutation check: re-deleting the
tombstone rows is the exact defect, and it returns both tests to RED.

### Coercion helper: NOT orphaned
Unlike dce2, which had to delete `_as_str_dict`, the boolean helper `_as_bool` survives. Checked
BOTH ways as instructed: Serena `find_referencing_symbols` returns ~25 live call sites
(`verify.*`, `mcp.*`, `identity.*`, `ui.enabled`, `ensure.hint_enabled`, and
`_config_sources._map_legacy_env`), and a string grep for `"_as_bool"` / `'_as_bool'` finds no
dynamic (getattr/monkeypatch/importlib) references. Its import stays; `make lint` passes.

### No behavior change — per-metric attribution
A byte-identical `rebar metrics` diff is not achievable, as dce2 also found. Baseline first: two
consecutive PRE-change runs differ in exactly 3 of 6134 flattened keys, all time-driven
(`bug_open_age_days` p50/p90/max).

Post-change vs pre-change: 13 of 6134 keys differ, and every one is attributable:
- the same 3 time-driven `bug_open_age_days` keys (baseline noise);
- `cost_per_accepted_change` (store-driven — ticket events moved during the session);
- `complexity_summary` per-file entries for exactly the 5 files this change edits, and only
  line-number shifts within them — no unedited file changed;
- `complexity_summary.functions` +2 and `total_ccn` +6, which is precisely the two new tests
  (ccn 3 each);
- `duplication_summary.percentage` by 3e-6, from the changed total LOC.

`module_size_distribution` and `oversized_module_count` are byte-identical. Critically, ALL FOUR
structural metrics still evaluate and still produce values — which is the point: the field
controlled nothing, so removing it changed nothing.

### The guard AC is MOOT
There is no longer a field that could regress to inert, so there is nothing to guard. Inventing
a guard here would be ceremony. Noting for the record that this AC depended on bug
2c58-e710-275e-4ff7 in any case: the current inert-config gate could never have caught this
field, because it matches bare attribute NAMES globally and `.enabled` is read on other configs
(`ui.enabled`, `LangfuseConfig`), so it passes without ever being read itself.

### Sibling sweep
Swept all 104 config dataclass fields for the same defect (declared + coerced but never read).
Two candidates surfaced and BOTH are live, read via a string rather than an attribute:
`ReconcilerConfig.lock_lease_secs` (via `getattr(cfg, "lock_lease_secs", 120)`, and it carries a
`# read-via:` marker) and `VerifyConfig.require_plan_review_for_close` (via
`gate_enabled(root, "require_plan_review_for_close", ...)`). No other inert field. Parity census:
`_commands/metrics.py` is the SOLE consumer of the `code_health` config object — no MCP tool, no
library facade, no automated caller reads it — so there is no second surface still offering an
off switch.

### Gates
`make lint` and `make typecheck` (mypy, 434 files) pass. The targeted suites pass. One unrelated
pre-existing failure exists on clean `origin/main` and is NOT caused by this change:
`tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present`
(the `metric` grounding backend is absent from the backend table) — verified by stashing this
change and reproducing it on the untouched tree.
